To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IARN is a model for recommendation that can learn user and item history dynamics in an interacting way and that it consistently outperforms the state of the art on real-world datasets.

we propose the IARN model that can selectively memorize the relevant history of users and items when making recommendations, and that our model can provide meaningful interpretations of recommendation results, and can be further enhanced by incorporating auxiliary information.

we propose an attention-based recurrent network to capture the joint effects of user and item dynamics over time on user-item interactions and that we demonstrate the effectiveness of our model by extensive validation on real-world recommendation scenarios.

how to learn a model to better capture user and item dynamics for recommendation.
the following questions: How to model the temporal dynamics of a user's preference over items? How to capture the dependencies between user dynamics and item dynamics in user-item interactions?
how to better capture the temporal dynamics of both users and items for recommendation, by jointly modeling their interactions.
